item.title: South Shore man charged with manslaughter following weekend shooting
item.description: Massamba Fall, 19, was arrested Monday night after an investigation by Montreal police into the death of 18-year-old Christopher Densky Damier.

item.title: Ssense reported over 200 layoffs last month to Quebec government
item.description: The fashion retailer also reported 20 layoffs in February 2025 and 72 layoffs in May, bringing the total count to 307 in the last year.

item.title: Gaping hole opens in Châteauguay bridge, triggers road closure
item.description: The Sauvagine Bridge over the Châteauguay River was abruptly closed on Wednesday after part of its deck gave way.

item.title: Quebec Liberals call for suspension of constitution process until after election
item.description: In a letter sent to the other party leaders and the two CAQ leadership candidates urging a common front, Charles Milliard says Bill 1 should be withdrawn so the process can start over on a non-partisan basis and include sweeping consultations.

item.title: Woman who drove into pedestrians and cars in LaSalle declared not criminally responsible
item.description: Kianna Mariah Sam of Lachine was facing six charges and remains detained at the Douglas Hospital.

item.title: Montreal demonstrators back regime change in Iran, thank Trump for strikes
item.description: Despite the deaths in the country, Mahbod Nazeri said the protesters' key message was: "The war isn't against Iran. It's for Iran."

item.title: Woman dead, 3 police officers hospitalized after exposure to toxic gas
item.description: Police believe there may have been traces of phosphine, a colourless flammable chemical, in the apartment.

item.title: REM introducing short-run trains terminating at Bois-Franc for test run
item.description: Some trains will run only between Brossard and Bois-Franc to prepare for Anse-à-l'Orme branch opening this spring.

item.title: Quebec faces family doctor recruitment crisis as graduates shun province
item.description: Quebec’s system for family doctors is discouraging new physicians from entering the field, Montreal’s association of family doctors warns.

item.title: Supreme Court can't consider whether Bill 21 violates rights, Quebec argues
item.description: In a rare move, Canada's highest court asked for arguments on whether the secularism law infringes on charter rights.
